stem: Two towns are 66 kilometers apart. Cyclist A leaves the first town riding toward the second town at a constant 18 kilometers per hour. Twenty minutes later, cyclist B leaves the second town riding toward the first town at a constant 22 kilometers per hour. How many minutes after cyclist A leaves do the two cyclists meet?
solution: In the first 20 minutes, cyclist A rides \(18 \cdot \frac{1}{3} = 6\) kilometers, leaving \(66 - 6 = 60\) kilometers between them.
Riding toward each other, the gap closes at \(18 + 22 = 40\) kilometers per hour.
Time to close 60 kilometers: \(\frac{60}{40} = 1.5\) hours, or 90 minutes.
verify:
t = symbols('t', positive=True)
hB = solve(Eq(18*(t + Rational(1, 3)) + 22*t, 66), t)[0]
ans = (hB + Rational(1, 3)) * 60
assert ans == 110
assert len(spr_answers) == 1 and Rational(spr_answers[0]) == ans
